newsitem.title: USA: TWA names interim CEO, operating officer.
newsitem.headline: TWA names interim CEO, operating officer.

text.p: Trans World Airlines Inc said Monday it named board member Gerald Gitner as vice chairman and acting chief executive officer.
It also named board member David Kennedy as acting executive vice president and chief operating officer, responsible for long-term marketing, planning and operation of the airline.
In addition, board member William Compton was named acting executive vice president-operations, responsible for day-to-day airline operations.
Gitner is chairman of Avalon Group Ltd, a New York investment bank, who has held senior management positions at several major airlines. He was employed at TWA from 1968 through 1974.
Kennedy worked for 26 years at Aer Lingus, where he was chief executive officer from 1974 until 1988.
Compton, a pilot for TWA, is past chairman of the TWA Master Executive Council for the Air Line Pilots Association. He has been employed by TWA since 1968.
TWA Chairman Thomas Meagher said the interim appointments are aimed at assuring continuity of senior management while the search for a new president and chief executive officer continues.
In October, Jeffrey Erickson said he would leave TWA in January, ending a two-and-a-half year term as head of the airline.

"We continue to seek the right candidate to succeed Jeff Erickson, and we have several qualified candidates under active consideration," Meagher said. "However, it has become apparent that the recruitment process may continue longer than we had originally hoped."

He said TWA was grateful to Erickson for agreeing to continue as chief executive while the search for his replacement proceeded, but added it was not fair to ask Erickson to postpone his plan to leave the company.
"These appointments will allow Jeff to keep his schedule and will assure continuity of management until a new CEO can be appointed early in 1997," Meagher said.
